L20: ## Kv9 Pilot Study
L21: 
L22: Purpose of study:
L23: 
L24: To assess efficacy and safety of Kv9 across a range of solid tumours.
L25: 
L26: ​
L27: 
L28: Eligible tumour types:
L29: 
L30:   * Soft tissue sarcomas
L31: 
L32:   * Mast cell tumours
L33: 
L34:   * Mammary gland tumours
L35: 
L36:   * Melanomas
L37: 
L38:   * Anal gland tumours
L39: 
L40:   * Squamous cell carcinomas
L41: 
L42:   * Other tumours may be considered
L43: 
L44: ​
L45: 
L46: Primary eligibility criteria*: ​
L47: 
L48:   * Tumour type diagnosed by fine needle aspirate or biopsy by a registered veterinary pathologist
L49: 
L50:   * ​Tumour smaller than 5cm
L51:   * Not receiving immune modulatory drugs
L52: 
L53:     * It is acceptable to be taking/receiving including apoquel, cytopoint, beranza or a recent vaccination
L54: 
L55:   * No wounds on the surface of soft tissue sarcoma tumours
L56: 
L57:     * Other tumour types will be a case by case basis ​
L58: 
L59: *See referral form for complete criteria ​
L60: 
L61: ​​​
L62: 
L63: Study protocol:
L64: 
L65:   1. Primary veterinarian to send through referral for assessment by Kode Veterinary Sciences (KVS).
L66: 
L67:   2. Additional testing completed as required.
L68:   3. Atleast two treatment appointments to receive Kv9 at treatment centres.
L69: 
L70:   4. A minimum of 9 revisits at primary care veterinarian or treatment centres over 2 years.
L71: 
L72: ​
L73: 
L74: Owner responsibilities:
L75: 
L76:   * You are responsible to schedule and attend all required visits  ​
L77: 
L78:   * You are responsible for the initial costs to diagnose your dogs tumour, and any other tests recommended by your veterinarian
L79:   * You are responsible to closely monitor your pet for any changes and update the clinical study team in a timely manner
L80: 
L81: ​
L82: 
L83: Financial support:
L84: 
L85:   * There is no cost to participate in the clinical study. KVS will cover the cost of treatment and monitoring appointments, and provide the Kv9 treatment free of charge.
L86:   * KVS will provide support to any participant experiencing adverse events during their time in the trial. If the event is suspected to be related to the Kv9 treatment, KVS will provide financial support, unless agreed to be excluded in the consent form.
L87:

L10: ## Immuvera Therapeutics and OMICA Biomed Strengthen Collaboration in Veterinary Oncology
L11: #### Immuvera Therapeutics (Norway) and OMICA Biomed (Spain) are pleased to highlight their growing collaboration in veterinary oncology. Together, the companies are combining Nebumet, Immuvera’s inhaled immunotherapy platform, with OmiCare AI, OMICA’s liquid biopsy and AI-based monitoring solution.
L12: 
L13: 【3†Image†framerusercontent.com】
L14: 
L15: Written by
L16: 
L17: Immuvera
L18: 
L19: News
L20: 
L21: Apr 10, 2026
L22: 
L23: 1-2 min read
L24: Nebumet is being developed to help prevent and treat lung metastases in dogs, while OmiCare AI is designed to support treatment monitoring through minimally invasive blood testing. The collaboration brings together therapeutic innovation and data-driven disease monitoring with the ambition of improving clinical decision-making, treatment follow-up, and quality of life for dogs with cancer.
L25: The collaboration is intended to support further development and validation of both technologies in a European clinical setting, while also strengthening the foundation for future regulatory and commercial progress.
L26: 
L27: Jørund Sollid, CEO of Immuvera Therapeutics
L28: “Our collaboration with OMICA strengthens the clinical and strategic potential of Nebumet. By combining treatment innovation with better monitoring tools, we are taking an important step toward a more integrated approach to veterinary oncology.”
L29: Agustín Arasanz, CEO of OMICA Biomed
L30: “This partnership demonstrates the real power of combining innovative therapeutics with advanced liquid biopsy and AI technologies. By aligning OmiCare AI with Nebumet, we are building a precision oncology ecosystem that can meaningfully improve outcomes and quality of life for dogs with cancer.”
L31: The collaboration reflects a shared ambition to advance more precise and integrated cancer care in veterinary medicine. By combining complementary capabilities in therapeutics, diagnostics, and clinical development, Immuvera and OMICA aim to expand the tools available to veterinarians and improve outcomes for dogs at risk of metastatic disease.

L10: ## Successful capital raise paves the way for pet cancer treatment
L11: #### Norwegian biotech company Immuvera Therapeutics has successfully raised capital via Folkeinvest. The company is now preparing for the final stage ahead of the market launch of an innovative medicine to combat cancer in pets.
L12: 
L13: 【3†Image†framerusercontent.com】
L14: 
L15: Written by
L16: 
L17: Immuvera
L18: 
L19: Insight
L20: 
L21: Jan 15, 2026
L22: 
L23: 1-2 min read
L24: Immuvera Therapeutics is developing a new drug to treat cancer in the lungs, a highly burdensome form of cancer with a fatal outcome. The company’s first product is based on the BCG vaccine, which is currently used to treat bladder cancer in humans. Immuvera Therapeutics has adapted the vaccine for use in the lungs and for veterinary medicine, initially in dogs. The dog’s lung tissue is treated locally, stimulating the immune system to attack cancer cells.
L25: The treatment is gentle and has the potential for high efficacy.
L26: The company has now completed a share issue via Folkeinvest, raising just under NOK 7.7 million. The share issue values the company at NOK 135 million post-money. More than 250 investors participated in the offering.
L27: 
L28: > “We are very pleased that so many new shareholders have recognized the company’s potential,” says Jørund Sollid, CEO of Immuvera Therapeutics.
L29: Significant unmet need
L30: There are more than 200 million dogs in Europe and the United States. Dogs develop cancer as frequently as humans, and every second dog over the age of ten gets cancer. As in humans, lung cancer is particularly difficult to treat. Today’s veterinary cancer treatment options are outdated and are either highly burdensome, insufficiently effective, or so complex that few choose to use them.
L31: Even though the total cost of treating cancer in a dog can quickly reach NOK 100,000, there is a clear and growing willingness among dog owners to pay for such treatment.
L32: > “Both dogs and dog owners deserve a gentler, more targeted, and modern alternative with fewer side effects,” says Sollid.
L33: 
L34: Proven technology and an experienced team
L35: The drug is built on well-established technology from human medicine and follows an efficient regulatory pathway. The company is led by an experienced team with expertise in business development, regulatory strategy, clinical studies, drug manufacturing, and comparative oncology.

L8: # Our Solution
L9: 
L10: Market Opportunity
L11: ## A One Health Opportunity
L12: 
L13: Cancer is one of the leading causes of death in dogs, and owners increasingly seek the same standard of care they would expect for a family member. Yet treatment options remain limited: surgery, chemotherapy and radiation are costly, not widely available, and rarely control cancer once it has spread.
L14: The same is true in people. Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death worldwide, and the lungs are a common site of metastasis. A therapy proven against lung metastases in dogs therefore addresses an unmet need in two species, through one programme.
L15: Market demand is growing rapidly as Millennials and Gen Z, now major pet owners, drive pet humanization and demand for advanced care, with pet insurance seeing significant growth now covering cancer therapy. However, pet parents face very limited treatment options relying on toxic, outdated chemotherapies as veterinary oncology remains decades behind human medicine.
L16: This vast unmet need, combined with growing One Health investment, creates the right timing for introducing safer, more effective therapy solutions to life-threatening disease in companion animals.
L17:   * Veterinary oncology is a ~$1.7B category growing toward ~$5B
L18: 
L19:   * One in four dogs develops cancer during their lifetime.
L20: 
L21:   * Insights from naturally occurring canine cancer can de-risk and accelerate human drug development
L22:

L25: Our Solution
L26: ## Nebumet: Inhaled Immunotherapy
L27: 
L28: Nebumet is an investigational, off-the-shelf inhaled immunotherapy for dogs with cancer that has spread, or is likely to spread, to the lungs. It delivers BCG, one of medicine's most established immune stimulants, directly to the airways as a fine mist, using a nebuliser. With multiple patent protections through 2045 and a clear regulatory pathway, Nebumet offers a compelling investment opportunity.
L29:   * Novel delivery of established immunotherapy with >30 years of human safety data
L30: 
L31:   * Proof-of-concept study (NEBULA) in 30 dogs with advanced oral melanoma, alongside a GLP target-animal safety study
L32: 
L33:   * Planned route to veterinary market authorisation

L27: ## Laboratorium Nanoonkologii Doświadczalnej i Klinicznej
L28: 
L29: ##### Nasza misja:
L30: 
L31: Pragniemy nieść pomoc zwierzętom cierpiącym na choroby nowotworowe wykorzystując innowacyjne metody badawcze (m.in. metodę simple western) i nowoczesne technologie (nanocząstki metali, głównie nanocząstki złota).
L32: ##### Nasza wizja:
L33: Prowadzimy interdyscyplinarne prace badawcze i rozwojowe, których celem jest wprowadzenie spersonalizowanej terapii nowotworów zwierząt z wykorzystaniem nanotechnologii.
L34: Nasze laboratorium to miejsce, w którym zespół pełnych entuzjazmu ludzi reprezentujących różne dziedziny nauki (lekarze weterynarii, biolodzy, biotechnolodzy) we współpracy z lekarzami weterynarii, lekarzami medycyny, chemikami, fizykami i ekonomistami z innych instytucji naukowo-badawczych każdego dnia dąży do wprowadzenia innowacyjnych rozwiązań dla medycyny weterynaryjnej i sektora biomedycznego.
